claims.text: A fine-grained, single-phase CoCrNiV multi-principal-element alloy can be prepared by rolling and heat treatment.
The constituent elements are uniformly distributed in the proposed CoCrNiV initial state.
V addition induces severe lattice distortion in CoCrNiV.
Systematically increasing V content will increase the magnitude of local lattice distortion in CoCrNiV.
Heat treatment can be used to modify local chemical order and the dislocation energy landscape in concentrated NiCoCr-type alloys.
Dislocation glide can locally break down short-range order during cyclic mechanical loading.
Local short-range-order breakdown produces a rejuvenated state with increased entropy and free energy.
Short-range-order breakdown creates localized soft zones in the matrix and near planar-fault boundaries.
The rejuvenated soft zones are intermittent and form specifically along dislocation paths.
Local lattice distortion is the cause of reversible short-range-order breakdown during dynamic loading.
The rejuvenated zones temporarily lower barriers to dislocation motion.
A rugged local energy landscape and elevated lattice resistance to dislocation motion contribute to alloy strength.
The combination of high lattice friction and transiently enhanced dislocation mobility balances strength and ductility.
Rejuvenated soft zones enhance strain hardening and thereby delay strain localization and necking.
Relative to a lower-V CoCrNiV baseline, higher-V material will have a higher strain-hardening rate and delayed necking.
Higher-V CoCrNiV will show more pronounced reversible rejuvenated zones and short-range-order changes than lower-V CoCrNiV during cyclic dynamic loading.
The proposed effect should persist only over the V-composition range in which CoCrNiV remains a single-phase solid solution.
Twinning and phase transformation can provide alternative hardening mechanisms and delay necking in CrCoNi-based alloys.
At extreme temperatures or substantially different strain rates, twinning or phase transformation may displace reversible short-range-order breakdown as the dominant mechanism.
In situ nanomechanical testing combined with 4D-STEM can directly detect rejuvenation and associated local structural changes during cyclic loading.
